newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens-led group to build Russian plants.
newsitem.headline: Siemens-led group to build Russian plants.

text.p: Siemens AG said on Monday a consortium it headed had won contracts to build steel rolling mills in Russia worth a total 400 million marks ($264.9 million), of which Siemens' share was about 180 million marks.
The consortium includes Schloemann-Siemag AG, Sket Schwermaschinenbau GmbH, Siemag Transplan GmbH, Netphen, Kieserling GmbH, Solingen, and Ebner Industrieofenbau of Linz, Austria.
The first of the mills, for fine and medium-grade steels, will be built at Stary Oskol, about 700 kilometers south of Moscow, for Oskol Electrometallurgical Combine OEMK.
The group will also extend another rolling mill built on the same site by Schloemann-Siemag and Siemens in the 1980s.
The rolling mill, with an annual capacity of one million tonnes, is due to begin operations in 1999. The bar steel will be of a high quality usable in the automotive industry.

The project will be financed by a group of German banks led by BHF Bank. Hermes export insurance cover has been granted. The credits will be repaid by steel deliveries to be marketed by Preussag Handel GmbH under a barter agreement.
